title: Fusion Innovation Bootcamp: Addressing workforce needs with unique educational opportunities
summary: Louise Ferris Yuqiao (Joy) Fan For decades, fusion energy has been primarily a scientific and engineering challenge, with much of the work focused on understanding plasma behavior, developing novel materials for extreme environments, and solving the technical questions that stand between a concept and a practical energy source. That challenge has not disappeared, but the field is in a state of flux thanks to recent breakthroughs, increased federal support, and growing private investment. We are at a turning point. As Oak Ridge National Laboratory’s Troy Carter wrote in a previous Nuclear News Leaders column, “over the past decade, fusion energy has moved decisively toward a credible pathway to a new energy technology” (NN, Feb. 2026, p. 10).

title: City of Hot Springs receives more than $340,000 Entergy Arkansas energy efficiency incentives in 2026
summary: The City of Hot Springs has received more than $340,000 in incentives this year through Entergy Arkansas’s Entergy Solutions CitySmart program, including $288,467.07 for energy efficiency improvements at the Davidson Wastewater Treatment Plant. Source

title: IAEA, Grossi give updates on Ukraine, Iran, North Korea, nuclear power growth projections
summary: Multiple updates have emerged from the International Atomic Energy Agency over the last several days, including the status of the Zaporizhzhia power plant in Ukraine and Director General Rafael Mariano Grossi’s address to the agency’s Board of Governors on Wednesday.

title: Norway Consortium Gets €1.8 Million Towards Development Of Nuclear Power For Maritime Industry
summary: Norway is moving a step closer to testing nuclear propulsion for commercial ships, with a consortium including shipbuilder Vard and offshore service vessel operator Island Offshore securing NOK20m (€1.8m, $2m) in government funding to develop an integrated nuclear power system for the maritime industry. The marine nuclear propulsion system (MarNuPS) project, led by Emerald Nuclear Norway, aims to move the technology from engineering studies into full-scale testing, with a first vessel deployment targeted for 2031 or 2032.

title: Bangladesh’s Rooppur begins supplying nuclear electricity to grid
summary: State-owned Power Grid Bangladesh, which is the South Asian nation’s only distributor of electric power, reported that Unit 1 of the Rooppur nuclear power plant fed electricity into the grid for the first time on Tuesday, November 17, with the initial output reaching 350 MW and lasting between 8 and 10 hours.

title: Sweden’s Skanska Completes Critical Demonstrator Project For Rolls-Royce SMR
summary: Swedish construction company Skanska has successfully completed an aseismic bearing pedestal demonstrator for Rolls-Royce SMR, marking an important milestone in the development of the British company’s factory-built small modular reactor (SMR) nuclear power plant. The demonstrator, constructed and trialled at Skanska’s Bentley Works facility in Doncaster, northern England, has proven the approach to producing the first-of-its-kind precast bearing pedestal offsite, Skanska said.

title: IAEA Team Welcomes Ageing Management Improvements At Japan’s Mihama-3
summary: An International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) team has welcomed improvements in ageing management at the Mihama-3 nuclear plant in Japan, but said the operator should ensure the adequate coordination and oversight of key activities. The team, which reviewed the long-term operational safety of Mihama-3, said Kansai Electric Power Company (Kepco) should also ensure the adequate analysis and use of external operating experience from external organisations in the area of long-term operation and improve the analysis and management of data for ageing management.
